curated.background:
Source. Erdős Problem 389 in the Erdős problems database; the page says the question was asked by Erdős and Straus: https://www.erdosproblems.com/389

Known partial results. According to the problem page, the minimal $k$ has been computed for $1 \le n \le 18$ by Bhavik Mehta (OEIS A375071); for example $k = 5$ for $n = 2$ and $k = 4$ for $n = 3$.

Status record. The status database linked from the problem page is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml , where the problem has the state open.

lean_target.correspondence: The proposition quantifies over every natural number n with n ≥ 1 and asks for a natural number k with k ≥ 1. The product of the k consecutive integers n, n+1, ..., n+k-1 is written as the product of n + i over i < k, and the product of the next k integers n+k, ..., n+2k-1 as the product of n + k + i over i < k. Divisibility is divisibility of natural numbers.
lean_target.text:
import Mathlib

def wishpool_target_prop : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧
    (∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (n + i)) ∣ (∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (n + k + i))

curated.name: The Erdős-Straus question on consecutive products dividing the next consecutive product (Erdős Problem 389, OEIS A375071)
curated.source_license: Licence of the source not determined on 2026-11-11; the statement is restated in the curator's own words.
curated.statement:
Question. Is it true that for every integer $n \ge 1$ there is an integer $k \ge 1$ such that

$$n(n+1) \cdots (n+k-1) \quad \text{divides} \quad (n+k)(n+k+1) \cdots (n+2k-1)\,?$$
